title: Decide on Movie/Episode type architecture
description:
DECISION: Protocol-based polymorphism with type unions (Option 4)

## Implementation Complete

Created MediaItem Protocol with shared interface for all media types:
- display_title: Human-readable title
- display_subtitle: Secondary display info
- file_path: Path to media file
- cache_key: Unique tuple for cache lookups

Added Episode dataclass alongside Movie, both implementing MediaItem protocol.

Created media_types.py with MediaType union and type guards (is_movie, is_episode).

## Rationale

Chosen for:
- Pythonic structural typing (idiomatic Python)
- Type safety with mypy compliance
- Easy extensibility (just implement protocol)
- No inheritance complexity (avoids dataclass issues)
- Minimal code duplication

## Key Advantage: Series-Level Context Sharing

Episodes from same series share translation context:
- Consistency: Same character names, places, tone across all episodes
- Cost savings: Only 1 analysis per series (not per episode)
- Better quality: Shared glossary maintained

## Files Modified

✅ subtrans/core/models.py - Added MediaItem protocol, Episode dataclass, Movie properties
✅ subtrans/core/media_types.py - Created type system (MediaType union, type guards)
✅ ARCHITECTURE.md - Documented decision with rationale and migration path

## Next Steps (Blocked Tasks)

Following tasks now unblocked:
- subtrans-6se: Update output.py to handle episode subtitle output
- subtrans-eza: Update selection.py for episode support
- subtrans-g4w: Episode dataclass implementation (already done as part of this task)

## Testing

All 135 tests passing ✅
notes: Architecture decision implemented: Protocol-based MediaType, Movie/Episode compliance, single-level episode context caching (per-episode context files). Future work split into separate bd tasks for two-tier contexts, merge_contexts, and CLI mode flag.

- Does NOT upload back to Bazarr
- Bazarr auto-discovers new subtitle files via filesystem monitoring

2. Is /api/episodes/subtitles for uploading or downloading?
3. Does Bazarr's auto-discovery work differently for episodes?

Possible outcomes:
1. Upload NOT needed:
   - Remove upload_episode_subtitle() from subtrans-6o4
   - Episodes work like movies (filesystem save only)
   
2. Upload needed for episodes only:
   - Implement upload_episode_subtitle()
   - Document why episodes differ from movies
   
3. Upload needed for both:
   - Implement upload_episode_subtitle()
   - Also implement upload_movie_subtitle() for consistency
   - Update movie workflow to optionally upload

Investigation steps:
- Check Bazarr API documentation for /api/episodes/subtitles
- Test if Bazarr auto-discovers episode subtitles like movies
- Verify if there are NAS/permission scenarios where upload is needed
- Consult with user about their Bazarr setup

Files potentially affected:
- subtrans/integrations/bazarr.py (if upload is needed)
notes: Decision: Upload NOT needed for episodes. Episodes work identically to movies - save translated subtitle to filesystem, Bazarr auto-discovers via filesystem monitoring. notes: Prefer protocol properties (file_path, display_title) to reduce Movie/Episode branching where possible; aligns with MediaType design.

title: Skip movies missing English subtitles from Bazarr list
description: Only list Bazarr wanted movies that already have English subtitles to translate from. In `integrations/bazarr.get_wanted_movies`, inspect the `/api/movies/wanted` payload and skip/log any movie that lacks an English subtitle entry before we display the selection table.
acceptance_criteria:
- `get_wanted_movies` filters results to movies that both miss Finnish subtitles and have an English subtitle present in `subtitles` (check `code2`/`code3`/`language`, case-insensitive); if English is absent or explicitly listed in `missing_subtitles`, skip it.
- Console logs each skip with the movie title and detected languages (e.g., `Skipping <title> - no English subtitles available (found: fr, de)`).
- `Movie.existing_subtitles` continues to store the raw subtitle metadata for retained movies; downstream path population is unchanged.
- Add unit tests in `tests/integrations/test_bazarr.py` that stub `httpx.Client.get` to return sample JSON and verify English filtering + skip logging; no real HTTP calls.
- Update README/CLI messaging if needed to note we only list movies when an English source subtitle is present.

title: refactor: split cli.py into smaller modules (2081 LOC)
description: cli.py is 2081 lines (5x over threshold). Split into cli_args.py (argument parsing), cli_ui.py (display/formatting), and workflows.py (phase1/phase2 processing). Improves maintainability and testability.

title: Allow user selection of MKV subtitle track
description: Let users choose which MKV text subtitle track to extract when multiple tracks exist. After discovering tracks in `processing.subtitles.get_mkv_subtitle_tracks`, display the options (id/lang/name/codec) and let the user confirm or pick a track; the chosen track drives caching and extraction.
acceptance_criteria:
- If no external SRT is found and there are multiple text tracks after filtering (non-PGS), list them in the terminal (table or numbered list with track id/language/name/codec) and prompt for selection. Enter selects the default (prefer the first English track if present, otherwise the first track); invalid input re-prompts or falls back with a clear message.
- When stdin is non-interactive, skip prompting and use the default selection automatically so automated runs do not hang.
- The selected `SubtitleTrack.track_id` is used for cache lookup/extraction; console logs which track was chosen. Single-track cases auto-select without prompting.
- Add tests in `tests/processing/test_subtitles.py` using monkeypatched `input` and stubbed `extract_subtitle_from_mkv`/`get_mkv_subtitle_tracks` to assert the chosen track id flows through and that prompting is skipped when only one track/default is used.
- Refresh docstrings/log output to reflect user-choice behavior and keep compatibility with any language filtering from the allowed-language config.
notes: Consider a helper like `choose_subtitle_track(tracks, default_langs=['en', 'eng'])` to encapsulate prompting/TTY detection. `SubtitleTrack.language` currently holds codes like 'eng', 'spa'; show `track_name` when present. Ensure the track id fed into `get_subtitle_cache_path`/`extract_subtitle_from_mkv` matches the user's choice to avoid reusing the wrong cache.

description: Update CLAUDE.md to reflect language-agnostic architecture. Update README.md with examples of different language pairs. Update all docstrings to remove Finnish-specific terminology. Add migration guide for users. Update comments in all affected files.

title: feat: merge series + episode contexts
description: Add merge_contexts(series, episode) with documented precedence (episode overrides). Use merged context in translation paths when both contexts exist.
notes: Merge rules from ARCHITECTURE: episode-specific entries override series-wide entries for characters/places/terms; episode tone/formality takes precedence; style notes should combine. Consider prompt updates to avoid duplicating series context and (optional) context_type field if needed.

title: Refactor subtitle detection for any source language
description: Rename get_english_subtitle() to get_source_subtitle() in subtitles.py. Add source_language parameter. Update find_external_srt() to search for any language pattern using _get_language_code_variants(). Update MKV track search to match any language. Update all callers.
